sources.title: Analyse de l’insécurité alimentaire aiguë et de la malnutrition aiguë, mai–décembre 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Current acute food insecurity May–June 2025; projection July–December 2025; response coverage January–May 2025.
sources.limitations: Dated multi-driver analysis; forecasts depend on assumptions.

sources.title: The Republic of Djibouti: Country Brief
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, Global Information and Early Warning System
sources.temporal_coverage: Rainfall and pastoral conditions March–May 2025; food-security projection July–December 2025.
sources.methodology: GIEWS country brief summarizes weather, rangeland and food-security monitoring for the reference date.
sources.limitations: A dated situation snapshot; seasonal forecasts and projected food-security outcomes are not observed results.

sources.title: Integrated Community Resilience Project (P506969), Project Appraisal Document
sources.temporal_coverage: Country context and refugee figures as of January 2025; appraisal and proposed project activities in 2025.
sources.limitations: Appraisal context and planned investments, not evaluated impact.

sources.title: Sustainable Management of Water and Rangeland Resources for Enhanced Climate Resilience of Rural Communities in Djibouti
sources.temporal_coverage: Six-year adaptation project listed as under implementation; page states intended results and target population.
sources.methodology: UNDP project page describes locations, climate risks, institutional needs and planned activities.
sources.limitations: Planned outcomes and targets are not evidence of completed delivery or independently measured impact.

claims.locator: PDF p. 4, table of current IPC acute food insecurity, May–June 2025
claims.paraphrase: For May–June 2025, IPC estimated Phase 3+ shares of 30% in Dikhil Rural and Obock Rural and 25% in Tadjourah Rural.
claims.limitations: Analyzed populations; multiple drivers, not climate attribution.

claims.locator: PDF p. 4, current IPC table; pp. 1–2, drivers and affected households
claims.paraphrase: IPC estimated May–June 2025 Phase 3+ shares of 50% in Markazi and 30% in Ali Addeh and Holl-Holl camps.
claims.limitations: Dated camp estimates; not climate-caused displacement.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 8–9, assistance coverage and uncovered vulnerable households, January–May 2025
claims.paraphrase: IPC reported 104,000 food-assistance recipients nationally, substantial coverage in supported villages/camps, and an urban coverage gap.
claims.limitations: Reported coverage, not independently evaluated outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 11–12, most-likely IPC projection July–December 2025
claims.paraphrase: IPC forecast July–December 2025 deterioration, including camp assistance reductions and rural heat/drought pressures.
claims.scenario: July–December 2025 IPC assumptions on assistance, prices and agro-climatic conditions.
claims.limitations: Expired conditional forecast; realized outcomes unverified.

claims.locator: PDF p. 1, rainfall and pastoral conditions, March–May 2025
claims.paraphrase: In inland pastoral areas of Dikhil, Obock and Tadjourah, March–May rainfall was about 50% below average; the brief says deficits impaired rangeland regeneration and pasture and water availability, worsening livestock body condition.
institutions: FAO Global Information and Early Warning System
claims.limitations: The brief reports a seasonal rainfall and pasture shock, not a climate-change attribution or measured conflict effect.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, refugees and food-security context
claims.paraphrase: The FAO brief reports 33,800 refugees and asylum seekers, most without livelihoods and reliant entirely on humanitarian assistance, highlighting limited buffers when food access deteriorates.
claims.limitations: The national total and livelihood description are a dated brief snapshot; it does not identify specific settlement-level outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The source identifies refugees and asylum seekers as people displaced across borders; it does not connect displacement to the reported rainfall deficit.

claims.locator: PAD p. 11, paragraph 6, refugee and asylum-seeker distribution as of 15 January 2025
claims.paraphrase: The February 2025 PAD lists refugees/asylum seekers in Obock, Holl-Holl, Ali Addeh and Djibouti-Ville; conflict and disasters are separate movement contexts.
claims.limitations: Historical registration and context, not climate-caused conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Separate conflict/disaster mobility contexts, not a causal chain.

claims.locator: PAD p. 13, paragraph 10, Dikhil regional context
claims.paraphrase: The PAD describes Dikhil's weak services, unemployment and aridity, with migration and climate vulnerability adding pressures.
claims.limitations: Overlapping pressures, not demonstrated host–migrant conflict.

claims.locator: PAD pp. 16 and 19–20, paragraphs 21 and 31–33, vulnerability targeting and project design
claims.paraphrase: The PAD proposes services and resilient infrastructure for vulnerable high-hazard locations, including refugee-hosting areas.
claims.scenario: Proposed project investments, not evaluated delivery.
claims.limitations: Appraisal rationale, not achieved risk or conflict reduction.

claims.locator: UNDP project page, project summary, locations, barriers and expected results
claims.paraphrase: UNDP lists a six-year project under implementation for 100,000 people, half women, in Ali Sabieh, Dikhil, Tadjourah and Obock. Planned activities include local early warning, water and rangeland management, and climate-resilient livelihoods.
claims.scenario: UNDP project targets and planned outcomes during implementation; not an evaluation of achieved coverage or impact.
claims.limitations: The page reports project targets and expected results; it does not report outcomes or conflict-sensitive implementation evidence.

claims.locator: UNDP project page, barriers and capacity-needs section
claims.paraphrase: The project page identifies gaps in technical/government capacity for water management and community landscape management, plus limited local and regional flood/drought early warning; these are stated constraints motivating the project.
claims.limitations: Capacity gaps are described by the project page as rationale; no independent assessment or measured baseline is provided.

search_audit.query: Djibouti drought flooding food insecurity rural regions refugee camps subnational vulnerability 2025
search_audit.outcome: Official IPC and FAO reports provide named-region rainfall, pastoral livelihood and food-insecurity evidence; the World Bank PAD provides named-site refugee and hazard context.

search_audit.query: Djibouti climate shocks pastoral livelihoods migration displacement conflict insecurity source report
search_audit.outcome: IPC and FAO connect weather/climate shocks with pastoral livelihoods and food insecurity; the PAD separately identifies conflict-related sanctuary seeking and climate-disaster displacement. No source inspected says climate caused conflict.

search_audit.query: Djibouti conflict insecurity displacement constraints climate adaptation water early warning delivery
search_audit.outcome: The PAD and IPC note conflict/insecurity-related displacement and service/resource pressures, but inspected sources do not establish that insecurity constrained adaptation or disaster response. UNDP describes capacity gaps without attributing them to conflict.

search_audit.query: Djibouti local resilience capacity pastoral water rangeland early warning project food assistance
search_audit.outcome: UNDP describes planned regional water/rangeland and early-warning measures; the PAD describes planned services and flood infrastructure; IPC reports actual assistance reach and urban coverage gaps. Project pages are not treated as outcome evaluations.

gaps: No inspected source explicitly attributes armed conflict or violence in Djibouti to climate hazards; the PAD names conflict and climate-disaster displacement as separate contexts.

The full Djibouti Country Climate and Development Report could not be read because the browser parser rejected its large PDF and a local retrieval attempt did not complete; claims rely on other official full-text sources.
The IPC projection and UNDP/WB activities are conditional or planned, not observed outcomes; IPC identifies assistance reductions and low purchasing power as important non-climate drivers.
No inspected source established that insecurity constrained adaptation delivery or disaster response; this is recorded as a search gap rather than inferred from displacement or service pressure.
